tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms (connection timeouts, one-way traffic, REJECT flows, slow transfers, DNS timeouts, NAT/EKS source questions) rather than internal implementation, and explicitly pushes applicability even when the user doesn't name the domain ('even if they don't name the problem'). It is a tight paragraph, not verbose.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a user is troubleshooting AWS network connectivity: a connection times out, is refused, or resets; traffic flows only one way; flow logs show REJECT... Also use it whenever the user shares VPC Flow Logs, a packet capture, or tcpdump, Wireshark, or tshark output, even if they don't name the problem.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps straight into domain-specific procedures (classifying evidence paths, querying flow logs, interpreting tcp-flags, etc.) without explaining general concepts like what a packet or TCP handshake is. It stays focused on non-obvious AWS/Wireshark specifics.
tests.evidence: Request ACCEPT plus response REJECT on the same ENI points to a network ACL (NACLs are stateless; SGs are stateful).

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body keeps detailed reference data (field definitions, query syntax, MTU tables, playbooks) in separate reference files, only stating core rules and pointers inline. No large reference blocks or conditional-branch data dumps appear in the body.
tests.evidence: Load references/vpc-flow-logs.md to interpret any flow log record. It holds the field definitions, flag values, address translation, and traffic that isn't logged.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All six files in references/ are linked via markdown links in the body (in Step 2A/2B/3 sections and the References list).

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is accompanied by a clear condition for when to load it, both inline and in the final References section.
tests.evidence: Load references/vpc-flow-logs.md: when interpreting any flow log record (fields v2 to v11, SG vs NACL inference, tcp-flags, address translation, unlogged traffic)

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All references use relative paths of the form references/<filename>.md with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (read-only commands, mutating-command prohibition, SG/NACL ambiguity) are prescriptive and exact, while interpretive judgment areas (labeling findings, choosing paths) give the agent reasoned criteria with explanations of why, matching specificity to fragility.
tests.evidence: Always write the read-only commands out in your answer, with the IDs or filters to use... Never claim certainty, and don't call either one "more likely" without configuration evidence.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: When presenting evidence-gathering options, the skill clearly frames Path A (query directly) and Path B (ask for evidence) as conditioned defaults based on account access, not an undifferentiated menu; within reference loading, a single appropriate reference is specified per situation rather than offering multiple competing tools.
tests.evidence: Path A: flow logs reachable in the account... Path B: the user has or must provide evidence.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable diagnostic approach (classify evidence, collect, interpret, confirm, self-check) applicable to any network troubleshooting scenario, not a one-off declarative task.
tests.evidence:

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes numerous environment-specific gotchas woven through the interpretation sections, covering non-obvious AWS/Wireshark behaviors that the agent would otherwise get wrong.
tests.evidence:
Some traffic is not logged, and SKIPDATA intervals hide flows, so a missing record isn't proof that traffic didn't happen.
Offload (TSO/GRO) makes packet sizes meaningless for MTU diagnosis in that capture.
